methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Growth → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.2x) to $10M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 8 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Emelody is a Growth-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Jon Thomas and Elizabeth Johnson that has raised $10M+. The valuation exercise draws from a sector universe of nine peers: one public company (277810.KQ) and eight private firms including Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Bedrock Robotics, and Dexterity.

Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.2x step-up multiplier typical of Growth-stage advancement to the $10M total raised proxy, yielding an implied valuation of $12M. Peer-median triangulation is not applicable here; while eight robotics and manufacturing peers exist in the broader sector, none satisfy narrow filtering criteria (same stage, adjacent stage, or similar valuation tier), leaving insufficient datapoints for a reliable comparable-company anchor. A sector-wide median would introduce unacceptable noise given the heterogeneity of robotics venture funding.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $10M to $14M, with a median point of $12M. This narrow range reflects reliance on a single method and highlights a material uncertainty: the absence of tightly comparable Growth-stage robotics assets in available data. Any valuation within this band should be stress-tested against Emelody's specific unit economics, revenue trajectory, and capital efficiency relative to the named peer set, particularly the private cohort. Additional transaction comps or internal financial data would materially improve conviction.
